text:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by trolls and lamias.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Far out in the Astral I once happened upon an island where eternal winter reigns. It is ruled by Yaver Arteia, a mad Arisen woman who calls herself the Snow Queen. Oh, what a vile hag she is, I tell you! I escaped from that island by a sheer miracle. The Snow Queen's favorite pastime is to abduct people and set them all manner of riddles. Fail to guess one, and you are turned into an ice statue! In her ice castle Yaver Arteia keeps whole galleries of ice sculptures that were once orcs, gibberlings, Arisen, humans... Her heart is as cold as her icy throne! That merciless shrew was all set to turn me into an ice statue too, and only by a miracle did I get away. Yaver Arteia must be stopped! If she simply killed people, fine — you'd rest a while in Purgatory, and that's that. But she turns them into statues. Just imagine: a man stands there, unable to move, to breathe, even to close his eyes. And so for a year, two, ten... Brr, how horrible. No, such cold-blooded torment cannot go unpunished! But reaching the queen will not be easy. Chill, a mad werebear shaman, faithfully guards his mistress's peace. And rumor has it that in especially fierce blizzards a huge bear named Helad appears on the island — though whether that is true is for you to find out.

Bosses: Helad, Sharptooth, Chill, Yaver Arteia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by Tekyans.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, that little island was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And then recently it was transformed as if by magic: now streams run there, trees bloom, there are even some little houses standing! I put in to shore, and more wonders: creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Something like gibberlings, but not gibberlings — fluffy and big-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they fear their kin may come to make war on them. I wished them the help of the Light, but they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. That island is a riddle, upon my word!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to discover the source of a great power near Umoir, and gave them a Knight to help — the warrior Claire Brightley. Arriving on Lumix Isle (as the island where that sorcery was being worked was called), they witnessed yet another miracle: instead of bare rock and ice, a settlement had appeared on the allod. And not just any settlement, but a village of the Tekyans, who had all perished — destroyed by Tep — and until then had existed only in the Illusory World. Yet these Tekyans were real creatures of flesh and blood. They remembered everything that had happened to them in Tequatl on Irdrich, but how they had come to be on Lumix Isle they did not really understand themselves. They wished to summon their patron Genlun, and to that end had built a statue of him. And Genlun did indeed answer the call, which, however, roused the wrath of Claire, who, being a Paladin, did not wish to have any dealings with a pagan god. Genlun related that a few days earlier something like a shining palm had taken them from Tequatl together with their houses and moved them here, while at the same time trying to erase all memory of their crocodile patron. Genlun sensed that there was another Tekyan village on the island whose people had already stopped believing in him, and he suggested going there. When the heroes and Claire reached the second village, it turned out that the Tekyans living there now worshipped the Light. But their faith was far from kind: to prove that the heroes were not pagans, these Tekyans proposed that they die and be resurrected. Not even Brightley agreed to that, so they had to pacify the fluffy zealots. Further on, the path through the village led them to June ruins, where the captive Klavdia awaited them. She revealed that it was her handiwork — both Lumix Isle and the Tekyans, whom she had managed to bring into the real world with the power of Tep's Spark. And the one who had taken her captive was none other than the Servant of Light himself, the fire-haired angel from Purgatory. Now the heroes and Claire had to fight him as well. What lay behind his displeasure, no one could yet say. But Claire decided to stay on Lumix Isle to keep an eye on Genlun and on the Light-worshipping Tekyans.

Bosses: Li-Ter, Plamennik, Fluffy, Claire Brightley.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Al Rihat Ruins.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by renegade Kanian sorcerers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

The Workshop? Why yes, I've heard of it... It's a strange place, I tell you. And an evil one.

They say that sorcerers of every stripe used to gather there to practice their arts in peace and quiet. They practiced until they began experimenting on Sparks — capturing them by force and moving them into other bodies. A regular branch of Tep's Pyramid. Naturally, everyone turned against the sorcerers at once — both the League and the Empire. Only the sorcerers had no wish to abandon their experiments, and threw everyone who disagreed with them into the Astral. Ever since, sheer devilry has been going on on that island. Those who have flown past say the sorcerers started felling the forest and building wooden soldiers and golems. And — just think of it! — that whole wooden army has come to life and seems to be preparing to attack our allods. That's where experiments with Sparks lead.

Bosses: Rustle, Burian Jagger and Gurrian Jagger, Yarosvat Zoriev, Porfiry Polenov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Until recently this rich mine belonged to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in fact the Mistress lives to this day in the depths of the island. If she wishes, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. Well, and she stopped wishing. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her due respect, only now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are countless, to be sure — only she guards them so that you can't get near!

Story allod:

For a ritual Velerad needed living gems — prophetic yakhonts, which could be found only on the island of Copper Mountain. It turned out that the island had once belonged to Goldie Nickel, but Goldie had lost it, and the new owner was his brother Zavid Nickel, a greedy, grasping man. Meanwhile disaster had struck the workings: something was frightening the miners to death, and they refused to work. The heroes tried to get to the bottom of it, and they had to pass a difficult path of riddles and trials to reach the local Sovereign — the Mistress of the Local Mountain. She punished Zavid for his greed by turning him to stone, but agreed to give a yakhont on condition that the mine be returned to Goldie and the way to her underground halls be forgotten. Alas, if anything in the world is immortal, it is human greed. Learning of the halls of the Mistress of the Copper Mountain, which were full of precious stones, people fitted out more than one expedition, breaking the agreement. After the ritual Velerad never learned where the Plague had come from. The visions were hazy and incomprehensible.

Bosses: Fire Jumper, Blue Yaga, Mighty Poloz, Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Addendum: The island was made on the basis of concepts by a player nicknamed Merani. The Servant of Light on the allod is a reference to her.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Many have heard the stories of the Silent Hills. An ancient evil awoke in that land, turning the peasants into will-less ghosts. They wandered their lands until brave heroes put an end to their suffering. But in the deep layers of the Astral the Silent Hills have a reflection. That is what an Imperial Warlock chose for his experiments. And he got so carried away that the horrors of old now seem like a children's tale. The villain destroyed the whole people and turned the good inhabitants into an army of the undead. Those hills are no longer Silent, but Dead!

Bosses: Cadaver, Guardian, Murderess, Sarang Fravashi.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, an industrial town of the Empire.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Metalville... A vivid example of what can happen to soldiers when they have a lot of free time not taken up by drill or reading regulations. Some ten years ago Metalville was a small mining town; then, when the mine ran dry, it was sealed and the town was handed over to the Imperial Army as a training ground. "Blues" against "Reds", just like in Igsh. And everything went strictly according to plan, until the general of the "Blues", a hulking orc named Gire the Merciless, quarrelled in front of all his officers with the general of the "Reds", Steel the Highlander. They swore at each other up and down, and parted ways. The "Red" had already forgotten the quarrel, but the "Blue" took such offence that he raised his regiment on alarm in the middle of the night and led it to the attack. He had decided to wash away the insult in blood! Under cover of darkness they hacked most of the "Reds" into mincemeat, and when dawn broke they realized that all they had to look forward to now was a tribunal and a firing squad by a brick wall. And with truly orcish stubbornness they decided to go all the way. Gire declared himself a great chieftain, the orcs the master race, and everyone else dust under soldiers' boots, and set about building his great Empire. But there was a snag: the astral ships had managed to leave Metalville. So now the newly minted chieftains of the Empire are stuck in the besieged town, fighting the remnants of the "Reds" and dreaming of a new orcish empire under the leadership of the great and wise chieftain Gire — curse him, the treacherous brute!

Bosses: Negus Mengulis, Rowdy Raja, Bubbah Two Fingers, Gire the Merciless.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Ammer.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a colony of the Aoidoi.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, the Aoidoi. They've only just come into the world, and they've already built themselves cities — for all to see. New Bay is only just being built, but it will be a beautiful city! You can't deny these stoneheads their courage, of course — the sector where the Bay stands is literally teeming with crazed monsters. Let's hope no disaster comes of it... I've heard, by the way, that some demons don't want to feud with them, but offer friendship instead. Hogwash, if you ask me. If the Aoidoi trust those creatures, they're as naive as children. Better be careful — demons are no joke.

Bosses: Agniy, Datura, Vile, Or-Khan.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Fenia's Island? Ah, that's the old Kanian fortress where those... what do you call them... right, I remember — the feminists! Or femmeists? Anyway, they're women who believe men wrong and oppress them, which has driven them clean out of their minds. No, you tell me — does anyone wrong women in the Empire? It's in the League that folk are completely savage; they even have a saying there, "a hen's no bird, and a woman's no person." Whereas with us she's every bit a person! Only our Imperial ladies run off to that Cloister regularly too... I don't understand why they've turned so against men?! Well, never mind, listen further. Their leader is some Fenia, a mad sorceress who proclaimed herself a goddess incarnate and the patroness of women. She announced that all the evil in the world comes from men, and decided to wage a merciless war on us — on men, that is! And the funniest thing is that some cracked heads actually believed her! Or rather, it was funny right up until they killed every man on the island, and the parts of their bodies — well, the ones that matter most to a man — they... All right, I don't want to talk about it. A friend of mine, Afanasy Nikitov, was there and saw it all with his own eyes. The horrors he told me... He escaped by a miracle! In short, there are no men in the Cloister now. Instead there's a crowd of women of every race, gone feral for lack of male attention and fanatical to the marrow, ready to tear apart any man who ends up on the island. Now there's a paradox — they hate men, yet without men they turn into beasts. No, I'll never understand women. Especially women who reach for a sword at the slightest thing and try to lop off what's most precious. Ahem. I meant the head, actually, not what you were thinking!

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by ogres and elemental spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Ah, Firefrost and its temple... An island where bitter cold and scorching flame exist in peace and harmony. A beautiful place! And everything that looks beautiful in the Astral is in fact deadly dangerous. I advise you to remember that, and to give Firefrost a wide berth. Before, only wild goblins and trolls lived there, but now, they say, the island has also been overrun by elementals. The cause, I suppose, is the recent eruption of a volcano long thought extinct. And they also say that over all of them stands a mysterious spirit, born of the two elements. I'd like to have a look at that marvel! In short, if you're not afraid of elementals and have no wish to live forever, you can find yourself a sturdy crew and give them battle. After all, it is an ancient temple, and countless riches must surely be hidden in it. It would be a sin to let such goods go to waste!

Bosses: Hestia, Bedlam, Blinder, Diamond.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, remnants of June mechanisms and ghosts of the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Young adventurers are firmly convinced that where there are June ruins, there are countless treasures. Seasoned heroes have learned that in ruins you can sometimes find a hoard, but more often trouble. And the most experienced know that most ruins hold neither treasures nor monsters: small wonder, since they have been there themselves and have already taken care of both. Is there anything on Altan Tepek? I don't know: the islet is placed very awkwardly, nothing but reefs all around. We sailed all the way round it, looked it over through a spyglass, but found nowhere to land. Still, it's a curious place: it looks like a tropical forest, yet there's snow everywhere, frost-covered palms stick up, and the wind howls over the frozen jungle. I thought I noticed some movement, but I never made out who it was: kobold marauders, maybe, or June undead. What, you want to dig about in the old ruins? Well, if you do manage to land, tell me afterwards who was roaming there and why everything froze!

Bosses: Frostmount, Jasper Defender, Metztlitotec, Ayateotle.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest creatures and spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

What questions you ask! I'd be glad to forget that island, but I can't...

Long ago Kanian druids brought a sprout of the Great Tree to a lifeless islet and turned barren stone into a truly magnificent forest. I happened to visit it, and I confess without hypocrisy — even in the Empire there are few places whose beauty can compare with that lovely sunny island as it was then. The mentor of the local pagans, the wise Dobroslav Radov, proved a most cordial host and received me, an Imperial, hospitably, disregarding all the differences between our powers! I flew away from the island with a friendly farewell and warm memories of birdsong, crystal-clear lakes, the most delicious birch sap and the rustle of thick foliage. And recently bad news reached me. A giant spider, a vile spawn of the Astral, crept up to the Great Tree under cover of darkness and poisoned it with its venom. All of Dobroslav's followers, and he himself, went mad. Now he is called Zlobinya Yadov, and nothing remains in him of the good-natured sage he once was. Now he and his servants offer bloody sacrifices to the Desecrated Tree! The whole island is overrun with venomous spiders, tirelessly spawned by their mother, Widixa. And Blackvenom himself hides somewhere in the dense forest. But if you tear out the hearts of the mad pagans and grant them peace by burning them in cleansing fire, Blackvenom will surely not be slow to appear. And with his death the blight will leave the forest forever. I beg you, cleanse the Desecrated Forest! Kill the Widow and Blackvenom, and perhaps the soul of the man I remember as Dobroslav will find peace...

Bosses: Widixa, Zlobinya Yadov, Yevstigney Volkov, Blackvenom.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Waterfolk Tribe.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

During one of the expeditions an island was discovered that had evidently broken away from the Holy Land. There is a place of power on the island, can you imagine! And the magic of the Light, over which the League and the Empire are fighting, is present there in full measure. The only trouble is that for the locals this miracle has become the basis of a bloody cult. They believe that the source of the Gift of Resurrection is the Scorpion King — a giant beast they call Serket. The Waterfolk and the Forestfolk wage war on each other and offer sacrifices to this scorpion. As you can understand, there can be no question of those poor wretches ever being resurrected. But, in the opinion of the island's inhabitants, this is how they guarantee resurrection for everyone else. This orgy must be stopped. However, the Waterfolk and the Forestfolk will not let you simply challenge their venomous king. You will have to fight them. The Waterfolk are stronger and more dangerous, so the main blow will fall on them. But your chief target is Serket, the Scorpion King.

Bosses: Waterfolk Priest, Gavial, Serket.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Based on the World Barque. Over time it was reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a goblin settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do you think of goblins? On the one hand, they are unfortunate creatures. Everyone makes fun of them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you just feel sorry for them. And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Nasty pests, always ready to do something low. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on Coba Plateau? There you go! There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect themselves this, what's it called... such a funny word... a president every year! For three terms running a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids. If in the course of your wanderings you manage to find this island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

Bosses: Goblin Overseer, Buzz, Urub.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a research base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I've never had occasion to visit Edge Isle. It got its name because it often appears near the Holy Land. No wonder the League and the Empire strove to capture it, to use it as an additional base. Our side proved quicker. But now access to the island is forbidden. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Edge has betrayed the Empire! Evidently there were demon cultists among them who managed to cloud the soldiers' minds. Or perhaps the whole thing is down to the astral worm that has dug itself in in the middle of the island. They say it can have a destructive effect on the mind. Elizaveta Rysina herself recently summoned me and questioned me about the heroes of the Empire. The thing is, at present our side has no way to send a punitive expedition to the island. And yet the traitors must be punished! And the island cleansed of demons!

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Based on the Hickut Shard (Enemy Nest).

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a Kanian hamlet.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Do you know the story of the Isle of the Damned? No? Well, it's not the kind of story you tell children at bedtime... A sad story, a bad one. A story about how the darkness in the soul is more terrible than the Darkness outside. On a distant island lost in the Astral there was a small village. Good people lived there, honest, hard-working. And among them were two young lovers, Ivan and Maria. They loved each other ever so dearly. When the time came they were wed, all proper and fitting, and began to live happily and prosper. That would be the end of the fairy tale... Only you and I don't live in a fairy tale. There was a certain man in that village, an outsider. A bad man, an envious one. He could not look calmly upon the newlyweds' happiness, upon Maria's beauty — and she was a lovely girl, the picture of health. He was terribly jealous of Ivan. Before the young couple were wed he kept making advances to Maria, and each time was sent packing, and a couple of times got a punch in the face from Ivan. And once they were married, he lost his mind altogether from black envy. He decided to destroy the young couple. By deceit he obtained Maria's wedding ring, the love letter Ivan had sent her before the wedding, and the bride's bouquet, which had stood unwithered after the wedding, and with the help of these things he laid a terrible curse on the young couple. From that curse both of them soon went to their graves. And so they were buried together. But the evil did not go unpunished — the curse fell upon the whole island, and the villain himself was not spared. He died and turned into vicious undead, and his cronies and accomplices became skeletons. The restless souls of the young couple remained in the grave, and there is no bright path for them while the curse lies upon them. I beg you — free the innocent souls, lift the curse! To do so you will first need to find the ring, the letter and the flowers the villain used for the curse and bring them to the young couple's grave, and then set their restless souls free. Well, will you take on this good deed?

Bosses: Heartbreaker, Shishimora, Korosten, Ivan Neladov and Maria Neladova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a demon hunters' base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

It's an ancient fortress, a venerable one. His-to-ri-cal! The Kanians built it even before the Cataclysm, when they were laying the Abatis Line — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids. How many times it was besieged, how many times burnt to the ground — and every time it was rebuilt. So it stood right up until the catastrophe, and then, together with other shards of the old world, it was lost in the Astral. And now, centuries later, the Demon Hunters found it — dilapidated, but all in one piece. Some say it was the courage of many generations of defenders that preserved it, others insist on an astral anomaly... Be that as it may, the Hunters rebuilt it, reinforced it with meteorite shards and turned it into one of their most powerful strongholds. Demons are afraid to sail within cannon shot of it!

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a hunting estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Cinderland... Yes, there's no other name for that islet now. And yet once it was the finest hunting reserve in the Empire! They say the Great Yasker himself liked to shoot ducks or run down a deer in that reserve. And the local forester, Kuzmich, was a fine drinking companion — sometimes we'd get so plastered with him that in the morning we forgot which of us was the forester and which the traveler. Hm, those were the days... And now there's nothing there but charred trunks sticking up and rabid beasts running about. Curse that mad Arisen Zem! And at first they received him as an honored guest. Why, an outstanding scholar had decided to pursue his research in the quiet of the forest! They arranged every comfort for him, you understand — a laboratory in the woods, peace and bliss. He worked away, clinking his flasks... But Kuzmich, kind soul, decided to find himself a drinking companion. He could hardly drink with the bears, after all? And he took to dropping in on this mage, to chat about science over a bottle or two. And Kuzmich's hooch is mighty strong! Kuzmich was fine, he has a cast-iron throat and a steel liver, but the wizard, blast him, drank himself into the horrors. And in his drunken state he went completely off his rocker, foundations and all. The swine set the forest on fire! He imagined himself the Fireborn, the Great Fire Mage, lord of flame, anchor up his stern! And that was it, the reserve was done for — for he really is a Great mage, so now the forest there burns but does not burn up, the animals blaze but do not roast, and the most terrible thing is that the spirit of the forest, old Oakwarden, fell under his spell and serves him. And Kuzmich has taken to drinking out of grief; he recognizes no one, just swills vodka without ever sobering up. I tried to bring him to his senses, but he punched me in the face and kicked me out of his hut, where a pack of fire wolves was already waiting. They chased me all the way to my ship and burnt such a hole in my trousers — it's a shame to say. At least they didn't singe my hide. So if you mean to pay a visit to the Cinderland that is left of the reserve, don't forget to take a fire extinguisher with you — believe me, it's blazing there good and proper.

Bosses: Kuzmich, Oakwarden, Volkh, Fireborn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Lower City.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a pirate base (fort).

Story:

Astral island:

Eugene Silberpod (Astral Adventurer):

Jolly Roger Bay! They say that a thousand years ago there really was a sea here, and a bay — and even then the Brethren of the Coast feasted here! Over his long life Feint plundered a great deal, and not just gold. Rare books, magical artifacts, ancient relics — anything your heart desires! Only he buried them in the most godforsaken spot. The living don't walk there, but the dead positively dance about. Do you know who they are? Feint's crew. He wasn't a mage, but he remembered the astral superstitions. They say that if you shove a black spot between a dead sailor's teeth, he'll never know rest, and will wander on until he gets rid of it.

Story island:

The pursuit of Klavdia led the heroes to Takalik Harbor, home of Eugene Silberpod, a slippery rogue if ever there was one. He agreed to escort them to the Bay. Jolly Roger Bay! They say that a thousand years ago there really was a sea here, and a bay — and even then the Brethren of the Coast feasted here! Over his long life Feint plundered a great deal, and not just gold. Rare books, magical artifacts, ancient relics — anything your heart desires! Only he buried them in the most godforsaken spot. The living don't walk there, but the dead positively dance about. Do you know who they are? Feint's crew. He wasn't a mage, but he remembered the astral superstitions. They say that if you shove a black spot between a dead sailor's teeth, he'll never know rest, and will wander on until he gets rid of it. Naturally, Silberpod wished first and foremost to get to the treasure. And this was not his first journey to the Bay; more than once he had tried to get the gold, but it never came into his hands. For the Plague, spreading from the portal to Umoir, had already begun to take hold of the Bay. Silberpod and his companions managed to capture the pirates' fort, and then they had to get through the traps and secrets Feint had left behind. But when they reached the spot where the treasure had been buried, it turned out that someone else had already moved it. The pirate was consumed by insatiable greed, and he ordered the whole island searched, including the cursed ruins. And there he came face to face with one of his old companions — Benny Cakeson. The power of the Plague had turned him into an unknown monster — and now the same fate awaited Eugene Silberpod himself, doomed to become the new guardian of Feint's treasure. The heroes set off through the Ancient Portal to Umoir... And the Bay met its own fate.

Bosses: Badyai, Merry, Shroud Weaver, Kraken.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by underwater dwellers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Underwater Kingdom? To this day no one knows whether it really exists. I'm not in the habit of lying, so I'll tell you what I know myself. I heard this story from a Kanian merchant. His name was Sachkov, or maybe Sadkov. He was a rich merchant, he was friends with the Free Traders, and they say he even had his sights on becoming an Oligarch! He carried goods back and forth across the whole Astral and spent all his life on the road. His wife, clever and beautiful, saw her husband once every six months at best, but didn't complain. And one day Sadkov's ship happened to stray from the caravan route. He saw a small islet — not even an islet, just a scrap of land with a well and an abandoned hut. And the crew was just running out of water. They put in to shore, and Sadkov went to the well for a drink. No sooner had he bent over than a cold hand shot out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! And a muffled voice from under the water said: "Promise to give me what you have but do not know of, or else I'll drown you." Sadkov took fright and foolishly promised to give what he did not know of. If you don't know of it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, and when the merchant got home he began tearing his hair out. His wife met him right on the doorstep with a little baby. The merchant was seized with horror — he had promised his own child to the vile water spirit! But it's not for nothing that merchants are taught to count first and write only afterwards. Sadkov remembered that he had last been home more than a year ago, and the baby wasn't even a month old! His dearest spouse's debit and credit didn't tally — the child turned out to be someone else's. Sadkov threw his wayward wife and the child out of the house to go wherever they pleased, and gave his clerk, who had stayed behind to mind the business, a proper beating — the child looked a great deal like the clerk. And from then on the merchant drank himself into a stupor and drank away his whole fortune down to the last copper. And when the water spirit came for his due at the appointed time, the merchant advised him to look for his pledge himself, and paid out the interest on the loan in kicks and cuffs. That's the sad tale. If you see a small islet with a well in the Astral — don't be lazy, throw a keg of explosives down the well, so that the wretched water spirit who drives honest people into poverty won't find life a bed of roses!

Bosses: Bereginya, Goldfeather Fish, Blackmarin, Sea King.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Zem.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Blood Countess... She who bathes in the blood of young girls to preserve her own beauty... Do you really want to hear this story? I'll tell you straight: it's disgusting. The Blood Countess's real name is Yasskul Bathory. I knew her personally — a pleasant lady and an outstanding researcher. But she had a thing about her appearance. Bathory, once the most beautiful of the rulers of Hickut, seized on any chance to regain her lost beauty. And, unfortunately, she found one... Thanks to her knowledge of ancient blood magic she was able to rejuvenate her body... and kill her soul! Hundreds of ruined women, rivers of blood steeped in terrible spells — that was the price. Bathory was outlawed and sentenced to death, but she managed to escape! Rumor has it that the Blood Countess took refuge on one of the astral islands. She has a whole estate there, with well-drilled and devoted servants. The horrors and debauchery that go on there would drive even a battle-hardened warrior mad! Beware the Blood Countess, if you don't want to become one of her slaves and end your life as a bloodless body on a laboratory floor.

Bosses: Yaver Nadashti, Rolling Hill, Mechanical Watchman, Yasskul Bathory.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: During internal testing of the island, an amusing bug appeared on it: a pigeon grew to the size of a boss. In the end it was decided to immortalize it and make it a mascot named Gosha. Now it can be met in various places across Sarnaut.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Zem fanatics and heretics.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

And how do you know about that, eh? That's classified information! The Committee will wring your neck for disclosing it! Oh, all right. Since you already know about the heretics themselves, so be it — I'll tell you in confidence. But mind, not a word to anyone! The Heretic Refuge is a stain on the reputation of all the Arisen. After all, it is from their people that all these dangerous madmen come! The heretics refuse to acknowledge the holiness of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believe that everything that exists arose from four elements — fire, earth, water, and nature as the union of all three pure elements. And they are so hardened in their heresy that they accept no arguments of reason. They bitterly hate everyone who does not share their faith. After several high-profile murders committed by this sect, the Church, with the full support of the Committee and of Yasker himself, anathematized them and opened a hunt for them. The heretics — or rather the handful that remained of their sect — seized an astral ship in port and vanished into the depths of the Astral. Time passed, and their existence was simply forgotten; all the documents were classified and sent to the archive. But not long ago a captain I know told me he had heard about the heretics from someone who had seen with his own eyes a man who had the misfortune to stumble upon their refuge in the Astral. That poor wretch barely escaped! His ship was scorched by fire, a hole from a huge boulder gaped in the hold, all the rigging was covered in mold, and half the crew had turned into ice statues... So if your adventures lead you to the secret refuge of the heretics, know this — they are mad murderers, and they will try to destroy you at any cost!

Bosses: Yasskul Flach, Negus Minhotep, Negus Haifa, Negus Zirach.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest fauna and an expedition camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Just a second, let me look in my notes. Hmm... Aha, here it is! An entry about a new island being added to the astral sailing directions, on which old June ruins were discovered. Right, right... In short, I know almost nothing about this island. It doesn't even have a name! According to our intelligence, a Kanian scout ship discovered, in the depths of the Astral, an island on which June ruins from the time of the rise of June civilization had survived. Since the ruins are of enormous scientific value, the League hastily sent a ship to the island with an archaeological expedition led by a certain Nastasya Zhmurova. The expedition reached the island and began excavating, after which contact with them was lost. The last message said that the scholars had almost broken through the passage to the central crypt of the June tomb. They also complained about kobolds that had turned up from who knows where. At present nothing is known of the expedition's fate. If you want my opinion — the scholars dug up what should not have been dug up. The thirst for knowledge, like the thirst for gain, leads to no good.

Bosses: Mamba, Capa, Twisthorn, Nastasya Zhmurova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Astral Graveyard.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, elementals, undead.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I had a friend — Roman Kuzin. A traveler, an explorer. And ill luck carried him to the Lost Isle. There has been no word from him since... The Lost Isle is a legend. The legend of a Pyramid of Tep that acquired a mind of its own and stamps out undead, putting Sparks into dead bodies. It is known that whoever manages to defeat the Pyramid will get a treasure. That is exactly what Romka dreamed of. He gathered information about the island. I will share it with you if you undertake to find this island and save my comrade. On the Lost Isle you will meet magical elementals that are the embodiment of the Pyramid's power. You will meet many undead created by it. By destroying them you will be able to reach the Pyramid itself, where you must find a way to switch it off. And if you do that and the Pyramid stops working, its treasure will be your reward. Well? Will you take on the job?

Bosses:

ver. 1: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Pyramid Guardian.

ver. 2: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Zinoviy Semetry, Crusher.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate; the climate on the shard is varied.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the dwelling place of the months and the seasons of the year.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The seasons... Long, long ago, when Sarnaut had not yet broken apart, these words meant more than a change of dates in the calendar. Nowadays, as they say, "spring is gone and summer's here, thanks to Yasker, never fear" — but back then the seasons changed on their own. Summer was followed by autumn, autumn by winter, then came spring and summer again. And so they went, one after another: one month decorously succeeding the other, neither lagging behind nor running ahead. But the Kanians have an old, old tale about a little girl who was lucky enough to see all twelve months at once! As if somewhere in the world there were a little grove where all twelve brother-months gathered once a year to discuss their year's doings. That's all old wives' tales, of course. Only a friend told me he had seen a strange islet in the far Astral. Like a glass ball, and inside it a grove with twelve fine young fellows. While they were flying past, the snow in the ball melted, grass peeped out, everything turned green and blossomed — and then in an instant turned yellow, withered, and the ground was dusted with snow again. They were just about to go closer, when — snap! — the island vanished as if it had never been. What do you think: maybe the tale told the truth? Maybe the brother-months are still alive, and that very grove is still intact?

Bosses: Winter, Spring the Fair, Autumn the Woeful, Bright Summer.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a haven of the Wormfaces.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Looking for treasure, are you? Heh-heh... There's no treasure there! Only sand, the blazing sun, heat and scorpions nesting among the ruins. As a Historian I know told me, there was once a huge observatory there, in which June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars and compiled solar and lunar calendars and the most detailed horoscopes. And now all that is left of the temple-observatory is ruins half-buried in sand. Not so long ago the Wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleared out some of the halls, repaired the old battle golems and jealously guard the ruins against any intrusion. Their leader, who I gather is called Mirage, desperately needs something in those ruins, and he will not hesitate to kill anyone who enters beneath the vaults of the old temple. Luckily I got away in time, or else my bones too would be drying in the hot desert sun now...

Bosses: Isides, Rattler, Horatrix, Mirage.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a holiday camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know, I know about that resort. The apotheosis of universal stupidity, not a resort. You know how scholars love to show off their technology and play at being conquerors of nature. Well, they took it into their heads to create a resort not just anywhere, but in the middle of the eternal ice. They found a suitable islet, freezing cold — terrible! They raised a dome there and built a whole little town under it. Imagine: all around a blizzard whistles, and inside the birds sing and the grass grows green... Bliss, in a word. Only our clever folk didn't take into account that a tribe of wild orcs lives in the caves there. They fed mainly on mountain goats and cave mushrooms. And when the engineers were building the dome, they sealed an underground stream in concrete. And the orcs were left with nothing at all to eat: the goats died off, the mushrooms withered. So they went to war with the resort's guards. And the guards there are first-rate, veterans to a man. No doubt they thought the big shots would be coming skiing. They made a great secret of it all — one step outside the perimeter and they shoot without warning. I wanted to unload some field rations from my hold for them, and they opened fire on me. Started blasting at an Imperial ship without a word! I barely got away. What secrets could they have there...

Bosses: Shakhrai-Gor, Pavel Syrin, Vyacheslav Lapochkin, Alexander Burdakin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret base.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's so hard to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they meant to open the gates — I don't know, and where they did open them — I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the personnel were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. You want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... Well, unless it's in a low voice, in my ear.

Story allod:

In the Plagot Ruins, records were found of a temporal anomaly that Skrakan himself had studied. Finding the coordinates of the place was no problem, and the petty crook and thief Urri Miloslavin reported that at the indicated spot stood a Xadaganian base, which Catherina had allowed to be built in exchange for certain Imperial technologies. Intrigued by this base, the heroes set off there. And it turned out that Gates-II was the testing site of a Time Machine built by the Xadaganian genius Alex Everykin. And Alex was ready to travel far into the past — for instance, to see the world before the Cataclysm. But when a temporal portal was opened into Zayan's tower, the heroes and Miloslavin found themselves in the past, while the Zayan of the past ended up in the future, after which the portal closed. What had happened threatened temporal paradoxes, but the heroes managed to find a way back. To return back to the future, they had to use the Grain of Protopower... Alas, on returning and giving the Grain to Zayan, the heroes learned that it was precisely the Grain that Zayan had needed to stabilize the spell known as the Great Experiment. And its loss had caused the Cataclysm to happen. Still, a question remained — was what happened inevitable? And Gates-II did not escape the sad fate that awaited all the Imperial laboratories. No one will ever tell now exactly where the Imperial scholars decided to open a portal... But it is known that the island fell victim to a terrible plague. Was it Tep's plague? Or something even more terrible?

Bosses: Hugger, Consumption, Rotgulp, Pandemician.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Tropical. Closest to the Kingdom of Elements.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by fire elementals and draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever heard of Volcano Isle? No? Then listen. Not long ago a tribe of draconids appeared on this island, worshipping a fire god who sleeps in the crater of a long-extinct volcano. With constant sacrifices the draconids kept him asleep, so that he would not awaken and his searing fury would not break out. But not long ago their high priest broke the established order and summoned the sleeper. The volcano awoke, and a mighty fire elemental burst out. From tongues of flame and the heat of flowing magma he created four guardians — huge fiery manticores, whose breath can burn anyone to ashes on the spot! If you decide to go to the island and try to awaken the sleeping flame, you must repeat the draconids' ritual, laying the fiery hearts of shellbacks on the altars. But don't even try to take him on while his faithful manticores are alive! The fire god put a particle of his power into each guardian, and with their death he will be greatly weakened. That's all I know about Volcano Isle. Good luck to you!

Bosses: Supreme Draconid, Bonesnapper, Hephaesto.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Temperate. Closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by sirens.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Have you ever heard the legends about the beautiful singing of sirens that lures the ships of hapless sailors onto the reefs? Well — those aren't legends, but harsh reality. On one of the distant islands an elven tribe has settled — I can't bring myself to call that rabble anything else. Astronauts report that songs and music drift from Sirens' Rock containing some evil magic that makes the crew steer the ship straight to its doom. Resisting the magic is hard, but possible, if there is a talented specialist on board. Though some deaf bruiser will do just as well. The amount of shipwreck debris around the island speaks for itself. It's hard even to imagine how many honest sailors have fallen victim to those bloodthirsty creatures! And where are they now, what have those creatures done with them? Eaten them? I have, by the way, reports of undead sighted on the Rock... I advise you to avoid this island at any cost. Although, by rights, of course, it's long past time to send a squad of adepts there to mow that scum down from a safe distance.

Bosses: Levoxia, Cock Pit, Ligea, Molpa and the Demon of Madness.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical. Closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Elven allod, inhabited by the remnants of the elves whom Catherina drove out.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A quiet little island, an inconspicuous one. Seven bogatyr brothers lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there — they had fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a little present. A marvelous mirror, a work of the ancient June — a golden frame, and the mirror itself of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that — expect nothing from them but some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it's downright frightening. Although... what if there are takers who'll want to get that mirror? For the bold, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

Story allod:

The elves began attacking the shipyard where the new ship "Eclipse" was being built, and generally getting in the way in every manner. The heroes had to be sent to deal with them. The heroes routed the elves, and it turned out that they were led by Alir de Tristesse. That same Alir who had been the head of the minor House of Tristesse and the father of that same Annette who had been Yelisseus's beloved. But the elf's mind had sunk into twilight — he only cried out gloomy prophecies. What had happened stirred Yelisseus himself — he had long searched for his beloved, and it turned out that the elves, on leaving Umoir, had gone to the Drowsy Woods. Without long preparation, Yelisseus set off. Alas, the Drowsy Woods proved a grim place. The Plague was raging there in full force, and nothing remained of the elven settlement but ruins. With a heavy heart Yelisseus found Annette's own diary. It emerged that the elf maiden had fled the persecution of her stepmother, the new wife Alir had brought home. And she had fled into the forest, where she found shelter with seven bogatyrs. Yelisseus set off to find them. When all of them had been found, the brothers told the sad news — Annette had died, killed by the machinations of that same wicked Baba Yaga. Yelisseus set off for revenge and fell into a trap; fortunately the heroes managed to save him and finish off the witch. And the cause, as it turned out, was a June artifact, the Mirror. It remained to say farewell to Annette herself. Yelisseus wished to see his beloved one last time as she lay in a crystal coffin. But when he reached that cave, the coffin was shattered, and out of it stepped Annette... Alas, the elf maiden had become a vampire. Yelisseus was full of resolve to save his beloved after all. "Stop! Don't destroy her!.. So that is what the accursed sorceress meant. Annette, my poor beautiful Annette! It wasn't enough for the witch to destroy the one fairer than she — the mad old woman decided to turn her into a monster! I don't believe it is all fated to end like this. If there is a way in the world to lift the curse from her, I will do it. But I dare not ask you for help again — this is my love and my burden. Leave us. And thank you for everything!"

With heavy hearts the heroes left the cursed island.

Bosses: Baba Yaga, Yelisseus, Annette de Tristesse, Evil Mirror.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Island size:

Small allods — the smallest allods, mostly a single settlement.

Medium islands — larger islands, usually with several large settlements.

Large islands — have many settlements and various zones and regions.

Climate:

Desert — deserts, not much vegetation, and palm trees.

Tropical — jungle and swampy jungle.

Temperate — meadows and forests of the middle latitudes, coniferous and deciduous forest.

Taiga — mostly coniferous trees and snow cover.

Tundra — small trees or none at all, permafrost.

Wasteland — a mixture of ordinary matter with the matter of another universe; also the astral wasteland.

Affiliation:

League — population of Kanians, gibberlings and elves.

Imperial — population of Zem, Xadaganians and orcs.

Elven — population of elves only; not part of the League.

Neutral — population from both the League and the Empire, Free Traders and pirates. And also various lesser races (Forestfolk, lizards, etc.).
